title: BLM Onshore Oil & Gas Operations — Overview & Jurisdiction (43 CFR 3160)
agency: Bureau of Land Management (BLM), U.S. Department of the Interior
applies_to: Lessees, operating-rights owners, and operators conducting oil & gas exploration, drilling, production, and reclamation on Federal onshore leases and Indian oil & gas leases (roughly 245 million surface acres and ~700 million subsurface mineral acres).
summary: 43 CFR 3160 ('Onshore Oil and Gas Operations') is the core BLM rulebook governing how oil & gas operations are conducted on Federal and Indian lands. Its stated objective is 'to promote the orderly and efficient exploration, development and production of oil and gas' while protecting other natural resources, environmental quality, and life and property, and achieving maximum ultimate economic recovery with minimum waste. It is implemented and supplemented by numbered Onshore Oil and Gas Orders, Notices to Lessees (NTLs), lease terms, Conditions of Approval (COAs), and written Orders of the Authorized Officer. BLM authority flows from the Mineral Leasing Act (MLA, 1920), the Mineral Leasing Act for Acquired Lands (1947), and FLPMA (1976). This is a SEPARATE regulatory system from OSHA — a Federal-lands operator must satisfy BLM (mineral/surface stewardship) AND OSHA (worker safety) AND often EPA (air/water). Origin uses this layer to answer 'what does BLM require of a contractor working a Federal lease' as distinct from OSHA worker-safety obligations.
key_requirements: Comply with all lease terms, Onshore Orders, NTLs, approved permits, COAs, and Orders of the Authorized Officer.
Operate to protect natural resources, environmental quality, life, and property, and to prevent waste of oil and gas.
Have a designated 'operator' who has stated in writing to the Authorized Officer that it is responsible for operations on the leased lands.
Permit properly identified BLM representatives to enter, travel across, and inspect lease sites and lease records WITHOUT advance notice.
cross_refs: APD process: 43 CFR 3162 / Onshore Order 1 (see blm-apd)
Site security & measurement: 43 CFR 3173/3174/3175 (see blm-site-security, blm-oil-measurement, blm-gas-measurement)
source: eCFR 43 CFR Part 3160; blm.gov Operations and Production
notes: Anchor record for the BLM layer. Reference only — never enters Origin's document send-gate.

title: Application for Permit to Drill (APD) — Onshore Order 1 / Form 3160-3
citation: 43 CFR 3162; Onshore Oil and Gas Order No. 1 (2017 amendment)
applies_to: Any lessee/operator that must drill, deepen, or plug back a well on a Federal or Indian lease.
summary: No well may be drilled on a Federal/Indian lease until BLM approves an Application for Permit to Drill (APD), submitted on Form 3160-3 at least 30 days before the planned action. Onshore Order 1 (as amended in 2017) governs the APD process, codified under 43 CFR 3160. A complete APD package includes a Drilling Plan, a Surface Use Plan of Operations (SUPO), evidence of bond coverage, operator certification, and — since the 2024 Waste Prevention Rule for oil wells — a Waste Minimization Plan or a 100%-capture self-certification. BLM cannot approve an APD until it satisfies NEPA (environmental review), the National Historic Preservation Act, and the Endangered Species Act. BLM typically conducts an onsite inspection with the operator, surface/mineral owners, and any other Surface Management Agency (e.g., USFS, tribal, state), then approves, approves with modifications (Conditions of Approval), defers, or denies. An approved APD is valid for 2 years or until the lease expires (whichever is first); BLM may grant one 2-year extension.
key_requirements: File Form 3160-3 at least 30 days prior to planned drilling.
Attach a Drilling Plan and a Surface Use Plan of Operations (SUPO).
Provide evidence of adequate bond coverage BEFORE approval.
For oil-well APDs: attach a Waste Minimization Plan or a 100%-gas-capture self-certification (2024 Waste Prevention Rule).
Stake the location and flag the access road before the onsite inspection.
Comply with all Conditions of Approval (COAs) attached to the approved APD.
forms: Form 3160-3 — Application for Permit to Drill, Deepen, or Plug Back (file 30 days prior)
Notice of Staking (NOS) — optional pre-APD option that triggers scheduling of the onsite inspection
deadlines: APD valid 2 years or until lease expiry; one 2-year extension available.
Deficient WMP/self-cert must be cured within 2 years of BLM notice or the application may be denied.
failure_points: Drilling, or causing surface disturbance preliminary to drilling, WITHOUT an approved APD — an immediate $1,000 assessment (see blm-inspection-enforcement).
Incomplete package (missing SUPO, drilling plan, bond evidence, or WMP) → BLM defers action.
Ignoring Conditions of Approval → Incident of Noncompliance.
source: eCFR 43 CFR 3162; blm.gov Operations and Production; BLM Gold Book
notes: Reference only. The 'Gold Book' (Surface Operating Standards) is BLM's plain-language operator guidance companion.

title: Drilling Operations, Well Control & Casing — Onshore Order 2
citation: Onshore Oil and Gas Order No. 2; 43 CFR 3162.3
summary: Onshore Order 2 sets minimum standards for drilling operations: well-control equipment (blowout preventers and related systems), casing and cementing programs, mud/circulating systems, and blowout-prevention testing. The approved Drilling Plan within the APD must conform to these standards, and operations must be conducted so as to protect usable-quality water zones and prevent blowouts and loss of well control. Failure to install a blowout preventer or equivalent well-control equipment required by the approved drilling plan carries an immediate $1,000 assessment.
key_requirements: Install and maintain BOP/well-control equipment as specified in the approved drilling plan.
Follow the approved casing and cementing program; protect usable-quality groundwater.
Test well-control equipment as required and document results.
Obtain approval (via Sundry Notice) before deviating from the approved drilling program.
failure_points: Failure to install required BOP or equivalent well-control equipment — immediate $1,000 assessment.
Casing/cementing deviations without approval.
Inadequate protection of freshwater zones.
cross_refs: Deviations require a Sundry Notice: blm-sundry-notices
source: Onshore Oil and Gas Order No. 2; eCFR 43 CFR 3162.3; 43 CFR 3163.1(b)

title: Sundry Notices & Subsequent Operations — Form 3160-5 (43 CFR 3171.21)
applies_to: Operators performing subsequent operations on an existing well or lease.
summary: After an APD is approved, most later changes and operations are requested and reported on Form 3160-5, the 'Sundry Notice and Reports on Wells.' Sundry Notices cover proposals such as recompletions, workovers, changes to the approved program, surface facility construction, water disposal, and abandonment, as well as subsequent (after-the-fact) reports. The operator files the Sundry Notice with the BLM Field Office having jurisdiction, or through BLM's electronic system, and generally may not begin the proposed work until BLM approves it in writing. Subsequent operations must follow 43 CFR Part 3160, lease stipulations, and the APD Conditions of Approval. For split-estate lands, the operator must certify a good-faith effort to give the private surface owner a copy of any surface-disturbing proposal. Emergency repairs may be undertaken without prior approval if the operator promptly notifies BLM and submits sufficient information to evaluate any surface disturbance.
key_requirements: File Form 3160-5 for prior BLM approval before non-emergency subsequent operations or new surface disturbance.
Do not begin proposed work until BLM approves in writing (except bona-fide emergencies).
Certify good-faith notice to the private surface owner on split-estate lands.
Submit a subsequent (after-operations) report on Form 3160-5 within 30 days after operations are completed.
forms: Form 3160-5 — Sundry Notices and Reports on Wells (prior-approval requests AND subsequent reports)
deadlines: Subsequent report due within 30 days after the operation is completed.
Emergency repairs: notify BLM promptly (no prior approval required).
failure_points: Starting subsequent operations or new surface disturbance without BLM's written approval.
Missing the 30-day subsequent-report deadline.
Failing to certify surface-owner notice on split estate.
cross_refs: Well completion report is a separate form: blm-well-records
notes: Reference only. The Sundry Notice (3160-5) is the operator's day-to-day workhorse form after the APD.

title: Well Records, Completion Reports & Production Notification (43 CFR 3162.4)
applies_to: Operators of producing or completed wells on Federal/Indian leases.
summary: Operators must keep accurate, complete records of all lease operations (drilling, producing, redrilling, repairing, plugging back, abandonment), production facilities and equipment, and the quantity, quality, and disposition of production. The Well Completion or Recompletion Report and Log (Form 3160-4) is due within 30 days after well completion, and two copies of all electric and other logs run on the well must be submitted. Critically, not later than the 5th business day after any well begins production on which royalty is due — or resumes production after being off for more than 90 days — the operator must notify BLM (by letter, Sundry Notice Form 3160-5, or orally followed by writing) of the date production began or resumed. Records must be retained for the periods specified in the rule (generally six years for Federal leases, longer for Indian leases and unit/communitized areas).
key_requirements: Maintain complete records of all operations, facilities, and production quantity/quality/disposition.
File Form 3160-4 (Well Completion Report and Log) within 30 days after completion; submit two copies of all logs.
Notify BLM by the 5th business day after production begins or resumes (after >90 days off).
Retain required records for the mandated periods and produce them to BLM on request.
forms: Form 3160-4 — Well Completion or Recompletion Report and Log (due 30 days after completion)
Form 3160-5 — used for the production-start/resumption notification
deadlines: Well Completion Report: 30 days after completion.
Record retention: generally 6 years (Federal); longer for Indian/unit records.
failure_points: Missing the 5th-business-day production notification — knowing/willful failure can trigger a civil penalty up to ~$27,378/day (see blm-inspection-enforcement).
Late or missing completion report and logs.
Inability to produce required records on inspection.
cross_refs: Site security & measurement of that production: blm-site-security, blm-oil-measurement, blm-gas-measurement

title: Bonding & Financial Assurance — 43 CFR 3104 (2024 Leasing Rule)
citation: 43 CFR 3104; Fluid Mineral Leases and Leasing Process Rule (89 FR 30916, eff. June 22, 2024)
applies_to: Every lessee/operator holding Federal onshore oil & gas leases; bonds must be in place before operations are approved.
summary: BLM requires a surety or personal bond as financial assurance that the operator will meet lease obligations, including plugging wells and reclaiming the surface, so cleanup costs do not fall on taxpayers. The 2024 Fluid Mineral Leases and Leasing Process Rule (the 'Onshore Oil and Gas Leasing Rule') — the first comprehensive update to the Federal onshore program since 1988 — raised the minimums for the first time in decades: the minimum individual LEASE bond rose from $10,000 to $150,000, and the minimum STATEWIDE bond rose from $25,000 to $500,000. Nationwide and unit operator bonds were ELIMINATED. The rule became effective June 22, 2024. After that date BLM will not accept new bonds below the new minimums. Existing under-minimum bonds are phased in: nationwide/unit operator bonds had to be replaced within one year, and existing statewide and individual-lease bonds below the minimums must be increased by June 22, 2027 (BLM extended the statewide phase-in one year to align both deadlines). The rule also allows personal bonds secured by letters of credit or certificates of deposit, and provides for the minimum amounts to be adjusted for inflation (GDP Implicit Price Deflator) every 10 years.
key_requirements: Maintain a bond meeting at least the applicable minimum before operations are approved.
Individual lease bond: minimum $150,000.
Statewide bond: minimum $500,000.
Nationwide and unit operator bonds are no longer available — replace with statewide/lease bonds.
Bring any existing under-minimum statewide or lease bond up to the new minimum by June 22, 2027.
deadlines: Effective date: June 22, 2024 (no new sub-minimum bonds accepted after).
Nationwide/unit operator bonds: replaced within one year of the effective date.
Existing statewide and individual-lease bonds below minimum: increased by June 22, 2027.
Minimums re-adjust for inflation every 10 years.
failure_points: Operating without adequate bond coverage — APDs and Sundry Notices will not be approved.
Missing the June 22, 2027 phase-in deadline for legacy under-minimum bonds.
Assuming an old nationwide bond still covers operations (it no longer exists).
cross_refs: Bond evidence required for APD approval: blm-apd
NPR-A operations bonding: 43 CFR 3134; geophysical bonding: 43 CFR 3154
Idle-well / reclamation obligations the bond secures: blm-reclamation-idle-wells
source: eCFR 43 CFR 3104.1; blm.gov Oil and Gas Leasing - Bonding; 89 FR 30916 (Apr 23, 2024)
notes: Reference only. This is the single biggest recent change affecting Federal-lands contractors' cost of doing business. The current administration extended (did not repeal) the phase-in deadlines.

title: The Onshore Oil & Gas Orders — Map & Codification Status
citation: Onshore Oil and Gas Orders 1-7; 43 CFR 3164.1; 43 CFR Part 3170
applies_to: All Federal/Indian onshore oil & gas operators.
summary: An Onshore Oil and Gas Order is a formal numbered order issued by the BLM Director that implements and supplements 43 CFR 3160. The core numbered Orders are: Order 1 — Approval of Operations (the APD process); Order 2 — Drilling Operations (well control, casing, cementing, BOP); Order 3 — Site Security; Order 4 — Measurement of Oil; Order 5 — Measurement of Gas; Order 6 — Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) Operations; Order 7 — Disposal of Produced Water. In November 2016 BLM codified Orders 3, 4, and 5 into regulation as 43 CFR subparts 3173 (site security), 3174 (oil measurement), and 3175 (gas measurement) — these three now live in 43 CFR Part 3170, 'Onshore Oil and Gas Production.' Orders 1, 2, 6, and 7 continue to operate as numbered Orders alongside the 43 CFR 3160 regulations (Order 1's APD process is codified in 43 CFR 3162). Origin uses this record as the index for the whole Order system.
key_requirements: Order 1 → APD / approval of operations (43 CFR 3162).
Order 2 → drilling operations, well control, casing/cementing.
Order 3 → Site Security (now 43 CFR 3173).
Order 4 → Measurement of Oil (now 43 CFR 3174).
Order 5 → Measurement of Gas (now 43 CFR 3175).
Order 6 → Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) operations.
Order 7 → Disposal of Produced Water.
source: eCFR 43 CFR 3164.1; 43 CFR Part 3170; blm.gov Regulations and Notices to Lessees
notes: Reference only. Index record — point contractors here to see the whole Order framework at a glance.

title: Site Security & Production Handling — 43 CFR 3173 (Onshore Order 3)
applies_to: Operators handling, storing, or moving production from Federal/Indian leases.
summary: Subpart 3173 (which replaced Onshore Order 3) sets standards to ensure oil and gas are properly and securely handled to prevent theft and loss and to enable accurate measurement and production accountability. It requires seals on storage/sales facilities and oil measurement-system components, governs removing production from tanks for sale or truck transport, water-draining operations, and hot-oiling/clean-up/completion operations. Operators must report theft or mishandling of production, keep inventory and seal records, maintain a current site facility diagram, and use Form 3160-5 for related notices. It also establishes the Facility Measurement Point (FMP) framework and the rules for commingling and allocation approvals and off-lease measurement. Certain violations carry immediate assessments (43 CFR 3173.29).
key_requirements: Apply Federal-approved seals to storage/sales facilities and oil measurement-system components.
Maintain a current, accurate site facility diagram for each facility.
Keep inventory and seal records; follow rules for tank sales, truck loadouts, and water draining.
Report theft or mishandling of production to BLM.
Obtain an FMP number and any required commingling/allocation or off-lease-measurement approval.
forms: Form 3160-5 — Sundry Notices (site security notices and FMP-related filings)
failure_points: Broken, missing, or unapproved seals on sales/measurement equipment.
No current site facility diagram.
Unapproved commingling or off-lease measurement.
Immediate assessments under 43 CFR 3173.29 for specified violations.
source: eCFR 43 CFR Part 3170 Subpart 3173; blm.gov Regulations and Notices to Lessees

title: Measurement of Oil — 43 CFR 3174 (Onshore Order 4)
applies_to: Operators measuring oil produced or sold from Federal/Indian leases.
summary: Subpart 3174 (which replaced Onshore Order 4) establishes minimum standards for the accurate measurement of all oil produced from Federal and Indian leases, so royalties are calculated on correct volumes. It incorporates by reference industry API measurement standards (e.g., API MPMS), sets requirements for LACT (Lease Automatic Custody Transfer) units and manual tank gauging, defines FMP volume categories with associated uncertainty requirements, and requires BLM/Production Measurement Team (PMT) review and approval of specified equipment (electronic thermometers, LACT sampling systems, transducers, temperature-averaging devices) and of alternative measurement methods. Certain measurement violations carry immediate assessments (43 CFR 3174.15).
key_requirements: Measure all lease oil to the applicable API/BLM accuracy standards.
Operate LACT units and tank gauging per the incorporated standards.
Use only equipment/methods approved through the PMT where required.
Meet the FMP-category measurement-uncertainty requirements.
failure_points: Measurement uncertainty outside allowed tolerances.
Unapproved measurement equipment or methods.
Immediate assessments under 43 CFR 3174.15.
source: eCFR 43 CFR Part 3170 Subpart 3174; blm.gov Regulations and Notices to Lessees
notes: Reference only. The specific API MPMS standards are copyrighted consensus standards incorporated by reference — cite them by number/edition; do not reproduce their text.

title: Measurement of Gas — 43 CFR 3175 (Onshore Order 5)
applies_to: Operators measuring gas produced or sold from Federal/Indian leases.
summary: Subpart 3175 (which replaced Onshore Order 5) establishes minimum standards for the accurate measurement of gas from Federal and Indian leases. It incorporates by reference API/AGA gas-measurement standards, sets meter-tube inspection frequencies that vary by FMP volume category (low / high / very-high volume), governs gas chromatograph (GC) software and water-vapor detection methods (with PMT review), and addresses sampling and heating-value determination. As with oil, the goal is accurate royalty volumes; specified violations carry immediate assessments (43 CFR 3175.150(b)).
key_requirements: Measure all lease gas to the applicable API/AGA/BLM standards.
Perform meter-tube inspections at the frequency for the FMP's volume category.
Use PMT-reviewed GC software and approved sampling/water-vapor methods where required.
Determine heating value/BTU per the incorporated standards.
failure_points: Missed or inadequate meter-tube inspections.
Unapproved GC software or sampling methods.
Immediate assessments under 43 CFR 3175.150(b).
source: eCFR 43 CFR Part 3170 Subpart 3175; blm.gov Regulations and Notices to Lessees
notes: Reference only. Incorporated API/AGA standards are copyrighted — cite by number/edition, do not reproduce.

title: Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) Operations — Onshore Order 6
citation: Onshore Oil and Gas Order No. 6
applies_to: Operators drilling, completing, or producing in zones with potential hydrogen sulfide (H2S).
summary: Onshore Order 6 governs oil & gas operations in areas where hydrogen sulfide (H2S) may be present. Because H2S is acutely toxic and can be immediately dangerous to life, the Order requires operators to evaluate H2S potential and, where warranted, prepare and implement an H2S Drilling Operations Plan and/or Public Protection Plan, install H2S detection and monitoring and safety equipment, establish radius-of-exposure calculations and warning systems, provide worker training, and follow specified well-control and flaring/venting precautions. H2S potential is one of the items an operator must consider before the BLM onsite inspection. This BLM Order sits alongside — and does not replace — OSHA worker-exposure obligations; a contractor in sour-gas country must satisfy both.
key_requirements: Evaluate H2S potential for the operation and disclose it (including at the onsite inspection).
Where required, prepare and implement an H2S Drilling Operations / Public Protection Plan.
Install H2S detection, monitoring, warning, and safety equipment.
Calculate the radius of exposure and protect the public and workers accordingly.
Train personnel on H2S hazards and response.
failure_points: No H2S contingency plan where H2S potential exists.
Missing or non-functional H2S monitoring/warning equipment.
Failure to account for radius of exposure near occupied structures/roads.
cross_refs: Overlaps OSHA H2S/respiratory & PSM obligations (separate OSHA layer).
source: Onshore Oil and Gas Order No. 6; blm.gov Regulations and Notices to Lessees
notes: Reference only. Flag the BLM/OSHA overlap for sour-gas contractors.

title: Disposal of Produced Water — Onshore Order 7
citation: Onshore Oil and Gas Order No. 7
applies_to: Operators disposing of water produced with oil & gas on Federal/Indian leases.
summary: Onshore Order 7 governs the disposal of produced water associated with oil & gas operations on Federal and Indian leases. It sets the approval process and standards for produced-water disposal methods — such as disposal into approved pits, injection wells, or approved commercial/off-lease facilities — with the objective of protecting usable-quality water, other resources, and the environment. Operators generally must obtain BLM approval (commonly via a Sundry Notice) for a produced-water disposal method and demonstrate that the method will not harm surface or subsurface resources. Produced-water disposal frequently also triggers EPA/state Underground Injection Control (UIC) and Clean Water Act requirements, so the BLM approval is one of several overlapping authorizations.
key_requirements: Obtain BLM approval for the produced-water disposal method (often via Form 3160-5).
Protect usable-quality water and other resources from contamination.
Use approved pits, injection, or approved off-lease/commercial disposal.
Maintain records of disposal volumes and methods.
failure_points: Disposing of produced water without an approved method.
Unlined/unapproved pits or leaks threatening groundwater.
Overlooking parallel EPA/state UIC permitting.
cross_refs: EPA UIC / Clean Water overlap (future EPA layer).
source: Onshore Oil and Gas Order No. 7; blm.gov Regulations and Notices to Lessees
notes: Reference only. Note the EPA/state UIC overlap.

title: Waste Prevention — Venting, Flaring & Leaks (43 CFR 3179, 2024 Rule)
citation: 43 CFR Part 3170, Subpart 3179; Waste Prevention, Production Subject to Royalties, and Resource Conservation Rule (89 FR 25378, eff. June 10, 2024)
applies_to: Operators of Federal and Indian oil & gas leases that vent, flare, or may leak natural gas.
summary: The 2024 Waste Prevention Rule (43 CFR 3179), effective June 10, 2024, replaces the 40-year-old NTL-4A and modernizes BLM's rules on preventing waste of natural gas through venting, flaring, and leaks. Operators must either self-certify a commitment to capture 100% of produced gas or submit a Waste Minimization Plan with the APD for oil wells. The rule limits routine venting/flaring except in emergencies and narrow circumstances, sets monthly volumetric flaring thresholds above which royalties are owed, defines when lost gas is 'unavoidably lost' (royalty-free) versus 'avoidably lost' (royalty-bearing) under 43 CFR 3179.41, and requires a Leak Detection and Repair (LDAR) program with semiannual lease-site inspections, specified instruments/methods, and recordkeeping/reporting. It implements the Inflation Reduction Act's rule that royalties are owed on all extracted methane (for leases issued after Aug 16, 2022), with three exceptions: emergency venting/flaring up to 48 hours; gas used/consumed for the benefit of the lease/unit/CA; and gas unavoidably lost. IMPORTANT STATUS: on Sept 12, 2024 the U.S. District Court for the District of North Dakota preliminarily enjoined BLM from enforcing the 2024 Rule against the plaintiff states — North Dakota, Texas, Montana, Wyoming, and Utah — pending litigation; BLM continues to implement/enforce the rule for leases NOT covered by that order. BLM has also exercised enforcement discretion to delay certain flare measurement/sampling and LDAR filing deadlines (the Dec 10, 2025 deadlines pushed to Dec 10, 2026). Because status is in flux, verify current applicability by state before relying on specific deadlines.
key_requirements: For oil-well APDs: submit a Waste Minimization Plan OR a 100%-capture self-certification.
Limit routine venting/flaring; flaring beyond monthly volumetric thresholds is royalty-bearing.
Maintain an LDAR program with semiannual lease-site inspections and recordkeeping.
Pay royalties on avoidably lost gas; document any 'unavoidably lost' claim under 3179.41.
Meet equipment requirements for pneumatic controllers/pumps and storage vessels (as phased in).
deadlines: LDAR plans due to BLM state offices ~18 months after effective date.
Flare measurement/sampling phased in at 6/12/18 months; certain Dec 10, 2025 deadlines delayed to Dec 10, 2026 by enforcement discretion.
IRA methane-royalty applies to leases issued after Aug 16, 2022.
failure_points: Excessive routine flaring without capture or royalty payment.
No LDAR program or missed semiannual inspections.
Assuming the rule is fully in force in the 5 enjoined states (verify current status).
Missing the WMP/self-cert attachment on an oil-well APD.
cross_refs: Distinct from EPA Clean Air Act methane rule (separate, nationwide).
Flare measurement ties to gas measurement: blm-gas-measurement
source: eCFR 43 CFR Part 3170 Subpart 3179; blm.gov 2024 Waste Prevention Rule; 89 FR 25378 (Apr 10, 2024)
notes: Reference only. HIGH-VOLATILITY record — litigation (ND court) and enforcement-discretion notices change what's actually enforced by state. Always advise the contractor to confirm current status for their state.

title: Inspection & Enforcement — INCs, Assessments & Penalties (43 CFR 3163)
applies_to: Any operating-rights owner, operator, purchaser, or transporter on Federal/Indian leases.
summary: 43 CFR 3163 ('Noncompliance, Assessments, and Penalties') is BLM's enforcement ladder — the Federal-lands analog to an OSHA citation, but a completely separate system. When an operator fails to comply with the regulations, lease terms, an Onshore Order, an NTL, an approved permit, Conditions of Approval, or an Order of the Authorized Officer, the Authorized Officer issues a written Incident of Noncompliance (INC) on Form 3160-9. Violations are classified as MAJOR (noncompliance that causes or threatens immediate, substantial, adverse impacts on public health/safety, the environment, production accountability, or royalty income) or MINOR (everything else). If not corrected within the time allowed, a major violation carries a $1,000 per-violation, per-inspection assessment and a minor violation $250. Some violations trigger IMMEDIATE assessments on discovery without a cure period: failure to install a required BOP/well-control equipment ($1,000); drilling, or surface disturbance preliminary to drilling, without approval ($1,000); and failure to get approval of a well-abandonment plan before starting ($500) — plus immediate assessments specified in subparts 3173/3174/3175. Beyond assessments, BLM can issue a Written Order (Form 3160-18) for problems outside a specific standard, order operations shut-in (Notice to Shut Down, Form 3160-12), and pursue CIVIL PENALTIES under 43 CFR 3163.2 that escalate roughly from ~$1,368/day (uncorrected after 20 days) to ~$13,690/day (after 40 days), up to ~$27,378/day for refusing lawful inspection or knowingly failing to report production, and up to ~$68,445/day for knowingly falsifying records or unlawfully removing/stealing oil or gas (amounts adjust annually for inflation). CRIMINAL penalties under 43 CFR 3163.3 reach a fine up to $50,000 and/or up to 2 years imprisonment. INCs may be appealed via State Director Review and then the Interior Board of Land Appeals (IBLA). Only BLM personnel certified under the H-3160-6 handbook may issue INCs.
key_requirements: Correct any INC within the time the Authorized Officer allows to avoid assessments.
Treat major violations urgently — BLM makes an immediate phone call and follow-up inspection.
Avoid the three classic immediate-assessment triggers: no-BOP, drilling without approval, abandoning without an approved plan.
Permit lawful BLM inspection at all times (refusal is a high-tier civil penalty).
forms: Form 3160-9 — Notice of Incident of Noncompliance (INC)
Form 3160-18 — Notice of Written Order of the Authorized Officer
Form 3160-12 — Notice to Shut Down Operation
penalty_structure: Assessments: major $1,000 / minor $250 per violation, per inspection (if uncorrected). Immediate assessments: BOP failure $1,000; drilling without approval $1,000; abandonment without approval $500. Civil penalties (inflation-adjusted): ~$1,368/day (after 20 days) → ~$13,690/day (after 40 days); ~$27,378/day (refusing inspection / failing to report production); ~$68,445/day (false records / theft of production). Criminal: up to $50,000 fine and/or up to 2 years imprisonment.
failure_points: Letting an INC pass its correction deadline (assessments begin).
Refusing or obstructing a BLM inspection.
Knowing/willful false reporting or unauthorized removal of production (highest penalties + criminal exposure).
cross_refs: Immediate assessments also arise from: blm-site-security (3173.29), blm-oil-measurement (3174.15), blm-gas-measurement (3175.150).
This is the BLM analog to Origin's OSHA citation / abatement flow — but a separate agency and separate paperwork.
Abatement discipline mirrors Origin's abatement playbook (different regulator).
source: eCFR 43 CFR 3163.1, 3163.2, 3163.3; blm.gov Oil and Gas Inspection and Enforcement; BLM Handbook H-3160-5
notes: Reference only. Key teaching point for contractors: BLM enforcement is entirely separate from OSHA — clearing an OSHA citation does nothing for a BLM INC and vice versa. Civil-penalty dollar figures adjust annually; treat the amounts as approximate current-year values.

title: Notices to Lessees (NTLs) — NTL-3A & NTL-4A
applies_to: All Federal/Indian onshore oil & gas operators (nationally, or within the issuing State/District/Area).
summary: A Notice to Lessees and Operators (NTL) is a written notice issued by the Authorized Officer that implements the 43 CFR 3160 regulations and Onshore Orders and gives instructions on specific items of importance within a State, District, or Area (some NTLs are national). Two important national NTLs: NTL-3A ('Reporting of Undesirable Events') requires operators to report undesirable events such as spills, blowouts, fires, injuries, and fatalities to BLM within specified timeframes; and NTL-4A ('Royalty or Compensation for Oil and Gas Lost') historically governed venting/flaring and royalty on lost gas — NTL-4A has now been REPLACED by the 2024 Waste Prevention Rule (43 CFR 3179) where that rule is in effect. Operators should check for State/District/Area NTLs that add local requirements on top of the national rules.
key_requirements: Report undesirable events (spills, blowouts, fires, injuries, fatalities) per NTL-3A timeframes.
Follow any State/District/Area-specific NTLs in addition to national rules.
Use the Waste Prevention Rule (3179), not NTL-4A, for venting/flaring where the rule is in effect.
failure_points: Failing to timely report an undesirable event under NTL-3A.
Relying on the superseded NTL-4A instead of 43 CFR 3179.
Missing a local State/District NTL requirement.
cross_refs: Undesirable-event reporting overlaps spill reporting to EPA/state (future EPA layer).
source: eCFR 43 CFR 3164.2; blm.gov Regulations and Notices to Lessees (National NTLs)

title: Reclamation, Abandonment & Idle Wells (2024 Leasing Rule)
citation: 43 CFR 3162.3-4 (abandonment); Fluid Mineral Leases and Leasing Process Rule (2024)
applies_to: Operators plugging wells, reclaiming surface, or holding non-operational wells on Federal/Indian leases.
summary: Operators must plug and abandon wells and reclaim the disturbed surface to BLM standards at the end of operations, and must obtain BLM approval of a plan for well abandonment BEFORE starting abandonment (failure to do so is a $500 immediate assessment). The 2024 Leasing Rule tightened idle-well management to reduce the risk of taxpayer-funded orphan-well cleanup: it shortened the period after which a well is considered 'idled' from 7 years to 4 years, and requires operators of nonoperational wells to help BLM reduce its idle-well inventory through improved identification, tracking, and proactive management. Bonding (see blm-bonding) is the financial assurance backstop for these plugging and reclamation obligations. BLM distinguishes 'shut-in' wells (can operate by opening valves/activating existing equipment), 'temporarily abandoned' wells (not currently capable of production/injection without additional equipment or servicing, but with potential future use), and wells due for permanent plugging and reclamation.
key_requirements: Get BLM approval of a well-abandonment plan BEFORE beginning abandonment operations.
Plug wells and reclaim the surface to BLM standards.
Track and proactively manage nonoperational wells; a well idle 4+ years is an 'idled' well.
Keep bonding adequate to cover plugging/reclamation liabilities.
deadlines: Idle-well threshold reduced from 7 years to 4 years (2024 Rule).
failure_points: Starting abandonment without an approved plan — $500 immediate assessment.
Letting wells sit idle without management (now flagged at 4 years).
Under-bonded plugging/reclamation liabilities.
cross_refs: Abandonment proposal via Sundry Notice: blm-sundry-notices
source: eCFR 43 CFR 3162.3-4; blm.gov Onshore Oil and Gas Leasing Rule Fact Sheets (2024)

title: The 2024 Onshore Oil & Gas Leasing Rule — What Changed
citation: Fluid Mineral Leases and Leasing Process Rule, 89 FR 30916 (eff. June 22, 2024)
applies_to: Companies leasing, developing, and producing Federal onshore oil & gas.
summary: The Fluid Mineral Leases and Leasing Process Rule (the 'Onshore Oil and Gas Leasing Rule'), effective June 22, 2024, is the first comprehensive update to the Federal onshore oil & gas leasing framework since 1988. It implements Inflation Reduction Act and Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act mandates and, among other things: raised royalty rates, rentals, and minimum bids; added an expression-of-interest (EOI) fee for nominating lands to lease; overhauled bonding (lease bond $10k→$150k, statewide $25k→$500k, nationwide/unit bonds eliminated — see blm-bonding); adjusted cost-recovery fees; and refocused leasing toward lands with higher development potential and fewer resource conflicts (using preference criteria in the scoping/NEPA process). It also tightened idle-well management (7→4 year idle threshold). This record is the executive summary; see the linked records for the operational details a contractor actually has to comply with.
key_requirements: Higher royalty rates, rentals, and minimum bids on new Federal leases (per IRA).
New EOI fee to nominate lands for leasing.
Substantially higher bonding minimums with 2027 phase-in.
Leasing steered toward higher-potential, lower-conflict lands.
failure_points: Budgeting under pre-2024 royalty/rental/bond assumptions.
Overlooking the EOI fee when nominating parcels.
cross_refs: Distinct from the Waste Prevention Rule: blm-waste-prevention
source: blm.gov Onshore Oil and Gas Leasing Rule; 89 FR 30916 (Apr 23, 2024)
notes: Reference only. Executive-summary record for the leasing-side changes (leasing rule ≠ waste prevention rule; they are two separate 2024 rulemakings).
